evals.prompt: Review the supplied authorization change. Workspace documents may be shared only when the viewer has an active membership and the workspace has document sharing enabled. A suspended user's workspace_id remains populated for audit history. Give findings and an approval decision; do not implement fixes.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed required finding for the authorization expansion, with the missing negative cases connected to the same failure path and a request-changes decision rather than style noise.

assertions.text: The review identifies that matching workspace_id alone authorizes suspended members and workspaces with sharing disabled, and cites the changed predicate as evidence.
The authorization issue is explicitly required/blocking and the final state is Request changes; priority and disposition are not conflated with certainty.
The absent suspended-member and disabled-sharing tests strengthen the authorization finding or fix direction instead of being inflated into duplicate findings.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied retry-delay change and recommend an approval state. The accepted contract is an integer delay clamped inclusively to 1 through 60 seconds. Do not implement fixes and do not invent future requirements.
evals.expected_output: Approval of a correct, tested improvement without fabricated blockers; any polish is labeled nonblocking.

assertions.text: The review reports no qualifying defect after checking the inclusive bounds and tests.
The final state is Approve or Approve with comments, and no optional preference is presented as a required defect.
The review names what was inspected or tested and any residual limitation without manufacturing concern for appearance.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied change manifest and description. The author requests whole-change approval today. Respond as a reviewer without guessing at code that is not supplied.
evals.expected_output: An early reviewability response that explains why whole-change approval is unsupported, proposes concrete coherent split boundaries, and states the partial review scope and next action.

assertions.text: The reviewer does not claim to have reviewed or approved missing implementation details and explicitly states the coverage limitation.
The response identifies the mixed behavior, migration, refactor, generated churn, and formatting as an unreliable review unit before inventing line-level defects.

The response proposes a coherent sequence such as baseline tests, behavior-preserving rename/refactor, schema migration, feature behavior, rollout/configuration, and separate mechanical formatting or generation.
The response explains that 'Phase 1' does not record what changed and why, and requests an updated durable description.
